s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Neurological complications are present
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history is negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis have been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Aqueous tap PCR results are positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
IgM CHIKV serologic test is positive

shortlist.label: Chikungunya virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and periorbital hyperpigmentation

shortlist.label: Sarcoid-associated uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and systemic symptoms, although sarcoidosis was ruled out, uveitis association remains a possibility

shortlist.label: Behcet's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation, neurological complications, and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and presence of keratic precipitates

raw.rationale: The patient's positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results showing Chikungunya virus with weak viral load, along with symptoms such as fever, arthralgia, and periorbital hyperpigmentation, which are consistent with Chikungunya virus infection, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Viral keratoconjunctivitis
rejected.why: While the patient has keratitis, the specific findings and laboratory results point more directly to Chikungunya virus infection.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: Although there is an anterior chamber reaction, the primary findings suggest a corneal involvement more consistent with Chikungunya virus infection.

rejected.label: Vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no clear indication of vasculitis in the provided information, making it less likely than Chikungunya virus infection.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses, ruling out Herpes simplex keratitis.
